lesson: On 2026-09-27 the npm `latest` dist-tag for `prisma` pointed at 8.0.0-rc.17 while `@prisma/client` latest resolved to 7.10.0. A plain install gave mismatched versions. Pin prisma, @prisma/client and @prisma/adapter-pg to the same stable version with --save-exact.

The Prisma 7 `prisma-client` generator is output to src/generated/prisma with moduleFormat="cjs" so that `nest build` (rootDir ./src, CommonJS) compiles it. Output outside src is not covered by tsconfig.build.json (include: src).

The BE spec only says `HomeSlide[]`; the concrete shape is in the FE spec: `{ id, image: AssetRef{ url, publicId?, alt? }, position }`. DB columns (image_url, alt_text) must be mapped in the presentation layer, and optional fields omitted rather than sent as null.
The plan to port business rules from the old Express app (docs/specs/BE_NESTJS_REBUILD_SPEC.md) is retired. Requirements now come from task briefs in docs/tasks/ and the owner's answers.

Query handlers return application views (interfaces next to the query), mapped from entities with toXView(). Presentation maps view -> response. The double mapping is accepted so application never imports presentation types.
In @nestjs/cqrs 12.1, CqrsModule.forRoot() returns global: true. Import it once in AppModule; importing bare CqrsModule in a feature module is not the documented setup.

queryBus/commandBus.execute() infer the result only when the class extends Query<T>/Command<T>. A plain class (or implements IQuery) gives any. IQuery, ICommand and IEvent are empty interfaces, so implementing them adds no type checks.

A handler must be in the module providers. Decorators only attach metadata; CqrsModule.onApplicationBootstrap explores providers and registers them. A missing command/query handler fails at request time with *HandlerNotFoundException; a missing event handler fails silently.

Publish domain events with eventBus.publish() in the command handler after persistence, not from the entity. Project.create() is also called by the record mapper on reads, so apply() inside it would emit false ProjectCreated events.

Errors in @EventsHandler handle() do not reach GlobalExceptionFilter, and the default publisher does not await handlers. Catch and log inside handle(); never rely on event handlers for the HTTP response.
class-validator @IsOptional() does not change the TypeScript type. Declare optional DTO fields as field?: T, otherwise the compiler assumes the value is always present.
The watch-mode start script is npm run dev (nest start --watch). There is no start:dev script.

A project must have at least one image (the cover). Enforced in CreateProjectRequest (@ArrayMinSize(1)) and Project.create(). Project.create() also runs on load, so a DB row with zero images makes the whole list fail as a corrupt record; toProjectView relies on projectImages[0] existing.

Project.create() also requires at least one image with coverPriority !== null (the cover). The repository picks the list thumbnail with orderBy coverPriority asc, take 1; in PostgreSQL NULLs sort last on ASC, so a non-null priority is chosen first. The DTO only checks the array is non-empty; the cover rule lives in the entity (DomainError), so a request with only null priorities fails there.

The cover-image rule is checked twice: custom class-validator decorator @HasCoverImage() (presentation/validators) gives an early 400 from ValidationPipe, and Project.create() keeps the domain invariant. A null coverPriority counts as absent because @IsOptional() lets null through.

Per project: cover images (coverPriority not null) are limited to 10 (PROJECT_MAX_COVER_IMAGES in project.entity.ts) and priorities must be unique within the payload. Non-cover images (null priority) are not limited by these rules. The DB unique (projectId, coverPriority) already allows many NULLs, so only the app layer enforces the cap. Duplicate imageUrl in one project is not validated and would hit the (projectId, imageUrl) primary key.

A project holds 1 to 20 images (PROJECT_MAX_IMAGES); imageUrl must be unique within a project and coverPriority a non-negative integer. Uniqueness across images is a rule of the Project aggregate (Project.create), not of the ProjectImage value object, which only knows its own fields. The DTO mirrors every rule with class-validator decorators for an early 400.

DTO validation answers can I read this request (types, nesting, presence, cheap bounds); domain validation answers is this a valid business object (ranges, formats, uniqueness, counts) and is the source of truth because it also runs when loading from the DB. Repeating a domain rule in the DTO is fine for early 400s; a DTO-only business rule is a defect. Limits must respect DB column types or Prisma errors become HTTP 500.

The owner allows the same imageUrl twice in one project (images go to S3 with a fresh key, so duplicates are rare). The application rule was removed, but project_images still has primary key (project_id, image_url), so a duplicate fails in the database and returns HTTP 500 until the schema changes (R-20261017-11).

Presentation may import domain constants and plain value types read-only (DTO limits, Role, Token); it must not call domain behaviour. Limits mirroring DB columns live as exported constants in the domain and are reused by the DTO decorators.

project_images now has a surrogate primary key id (uuid, database default gen_random_uuid()), replacing (project_id, image_url), so the same imageUrl may repeat within a project. Use dbgenerated for the default so raw SQL seeds work; uuid(7) in Prisma is client-side only. The unique (project_id, cover_priority) remains and doubles as the project_id index. Migration 20261017120000 is written but must be applied by the owner.

CommandBus.execute() calls publisher.publish(command) and then the handler found in its own map, so a custom commandPublisher cannot break command handling (LoggingCommandPublisher is the example in app.module.ts). Events differ: handlers listen on the default publisher subject. Also, @nestjs/testing uses a logger that prints only errors; call app.useLogger(new ConsoleLogger()) to see Logger.log output in a test app.

ProjectCreatedEvent(name, projectId) was published as (project.id, project.name). Two string parameters in a different order compile fine and silently swap data. Prefer one props object or distinct branded types for events with several strings.

Transactions: handler calls TransactionManager.run(() => work) (port in shared/domain, PrismaTransactionManager in src/database), tx travels in an AsyncLocalStorage (transaction-context.ts), repositories read it through a db getter (getTx() ?? this._prisma). A repository that keeps using this._prisma writes outside the transaction silently. Pass run a function, not its result. Events are published after run returns. Provider classes need @Injectable() or constructor dependencies are undefined at runtime while the build stays green.

Project list reads through ProjectQueryRepository (domain port) returning the ProjectSummary read model, not entities: only needed columns are selected, Project.create() does not run, and the Prisma select result is structurally assignable to the plain domain interface so no record mapper is needed. The port must not import Prisma types. The application layer still maps ProjectSummary to ProjectView; projectImages[0] may be undefined because no entity guarantees an image. Reference: reflective-andon-api splits commands/queries repositories the same way.
